# cancho-gpu

> lex-gpu's .lx tile-kernel compiler, written in cancho: it checks a typed tile program (linearity, bounds, shapes, the threadgroup budget) and lowers it to CUDA C and Metal, byte-identical with lex-gpu's Rust emitter on 140 cases (116 emit, 24 refused by both). It links only libc; its authority report names what it may do (args, stderr, file read and write, heap, stdout) and no network or foreign code. Alpha: the compiler and device path are built; the inference runtime is under way.

## Use it
- [Quick start](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu#quick-start): build the compiler at the pinned revision, emit a kernel.
- Commands: `cancho-gpu emit <file.lx> <dir> [name=value ...] [--run]`, `cancho-gpu check <file.lx> [name=value ...] [--run]`, `cancho-gpu gguf <file.gguf> [--sum]`. A refusal is `error[<rule>]: <message>` on stderr, exit 1; a usage mistake is exit 2.

## Facts that matter when calling it
- Targets: nvidia-ada (CUDA C) and apple-m-series (Metal), each from the file's schedule. amd-cdna3 is a schedule row with no emitter.
- Device paths: Metal has run on Apple Silicon (reach and numerical agreement, not speed). CUDA is verified against a mock driver only; no real NVIDIA GPU run yet.
- `gguf` reads the first 32 MiB of a file: metadata and tensor directory, never tensor values. It refuses hostile input with a rule tag (gguf-truncated, gguf-version, gguf-duplicate, ...).
- Not implemented: tokenizer, sampler, serving layer, model adapters, AMD, Hopper.
